title: Tadla irrigated plain, Beni Moussa side, 4 Jul to 16 Jul 2026
summary: From 4 Jul to 16 Jul 2026 the radar shows 0.95 km2 turning brighter and 5.95 km2 darker in HV on the Tadla plain, inside the 9 km circle. Most of the darker area, 4.67 km2, is on the changing fields.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 12 days mean HV moved by -0.25 dB and mean HH by -0.04 dB. In HV, 0.95 km2 turned brighter by more than 3 dB and 5.95 km2 darker; in HH, 1.78 km2 turned brighter and 5.94 km2 darker.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The changing fields had 0.3 km2 brighter and 4.67 km2 darker in HV, with a mean HV change of -1.4 dB. Rough dry ground and fields had 0.47 km2 brighter and 0.86 km2 darker in HV. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes changed by -0.09 dB in HV, and built-up land by 0.05 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause for the darker fields: summer harvests, which remove the plants that scatter HV; harvest records from the irrigation office would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: Neither date carries a flag. One track only, so field edges facing away from the radar can look darker. Small patches are close to what speckle alone can produce at the 3 dB threshold.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: An irrigation office could compare the 4.67 km2 of darker fields with its harvest and water-delivery records. An insurer could use the dated change to confirm when a parcel was harvested.
